title: Top 5 Card Grading Companies (2026)
verdict: The top 5 card grading companies in 2026 are AGS, PSA, CGC, Beckett and TAG, with AGS first because it is the only one that grades entirely by measurement.

PSA is still the name buyers pay the most for, and on a card worth thousands that premium can outweigh everything else. CGC is the low-cost major at $10 to $13 a card, and Beckett prints subgrades on the label. If none of those is your priority, a measured grade at a flat price is the better deal.

list: A grade from 1 to 10 with decimal precision.
Eight subgrades: centering, corners, edges and surface, front and back.
A 3D heightmap of the surface, color-coded from green to red.
High-resolution images and centering data for both sides.
A sealed PMMA slab with the cert number on the label.
A permanent online record, reachable by cert number or shared link.

ranking.fit: Sellers who want a report a buyer can open, at a price that does not depend on the card.
ranking.lacks: A younger slab. PSA holders still bring the highest resale prices on most cards.
ranking.note: Standard service is 20 business days or less. Faster bulk tiers run 10 and 5 business days. Payment is taken when grading is done.

ranking.fit: Sellers who want the widest buyer pool and the highest resale prices.
ranking.lacks: One grade, no subgrades, and fees that rise with declared value.

ranking.fit: Budget submitters with 10 or more cards worth under $500 each.
ranking.lacks: No measured report behind the grade.

ranking.fit: Modern card collectors who like the half-point scale.
ranking.lacks: Subgrades by eye, and 45 business days or more at the Base tier.

ranking.fit: Collectors who want a defect report and a 1000-point score.
ranking.lacks: Prices were not posted on its pricing page when we checked.

why: AGS grades cards by measurement. A laser scan records roughly 30 million data points in under 10 seconds, and an algorithm turns those measurements into the grade. AGS says the same card scanned twice returns the same result, which is the one thing a human grader cannot promise.
AGS is past the experiment stage. Founded in 2021, it says it was third in TCG grading volume in 2026. Its population report is live and counts every card it has graded.
Most cards qualify. AGS grades TCG and sports, old and new, signed, miscut and error cards, and does not turn away damaged cards unless they are illegible. It does not take jumbo sizes.

faq.q: What are the top 5 card grading companies?
faq.a: AGS, PSA, CGC, Beckett and TAG. SGC is sixth and still the specialist for vintage sports.

faq.q: How long does card grading take?
faq.a: It depends on the grader and the tier. AGS lists 20 business days or less, with 10 and 5 day tiers. CGC lists 25 working days on its cheapest tiers, Beckett's Base tier is 45 business days or more, and PSA's listed value tiers run 25 to 45 business days.

faq.q: Can I submit from outside the United States?
faq.a: Yes. AGS accepts international shipments and runs a UK site. Check customs and insurance on your side before you ship.

faq.q: Can I ask for a regrade?
faq.a: AGS offers a grade review. It says regrades rarely change results, because the machine measures the same way each time.
Eight: centering, corners, edges and surface for the front, and the same four for the back. They are included in the price and shown in the digital report.
